title: The Easiest Way To Improve Classroom Behavior https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2015/04/25/the-easiest-way-to-improve-classroom-behavior/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Michael Linsin proposes politeness as an underrated but highly effective classroom management strategy, one requiring no drastic changes, extra planning, or special training. He recommends teaching three foundational areas—please and thank you, hello and goodbye, and excuse me and after you—through modeling, guided practice with common classroom scenarios, and gentle in-the-moment reminders like a whispered 'please' or 'excuse me.' Linsin insists the teacher must be the primary role model of politeness at all times, since sarcasm, impatience, or grouchiness undoes the benefits. He frames the strategy as simple, easily overlooked, and perhaps unfashionable, but ultimately transformative for classroom tone and behavior when applied consistently.
points: Politeness is presented as an underused, low-effort strategy that produces substantial improvements in classroom behavior and tone.
Three foundational areas to teach explicitly: please and thank you, hello and goodbye, and excuse me and after you.
The teaching method involves modeling scenarios (greeting a classmate, accepting help, letting someone pass), then breaking students into groups to role-play common situations.
Ongoing reinforcement comes through brief, gentle stage-whispered cues ('please,' 'good morning,' 'excuse me') rather than lengthy lessons.
The teacher must model politeness consistently, since sarcasm, impatience, or grouchiness on the teacher's part can undo the strategy's benefits.
quotes: The easiest way to improve classroom behavior is one few teachers ever consider.
It doesn’t entail making drastic changes. It doesn’t entail extra planning or specialized training.
Walk into any polite classroom anywhere in the world and there you will find well-behaved students.
These three alone will change the tone of your classroom, inspire more profound acts of kindness, and result in better overall classroom behavior.
But you must be the leader, the chief role model, the pillar of politeness. Every day. Sarcasm, impatience, and grouchiness will undo any good vibrations you’ve created.
Teaching politeness is a simple little thing. Easily disregarded, quickly forgotten, and too 1950s for today’s educational complexities.
